## Best first contact: **American WCL**

I’d contact **American University Washington College of Law (WCL) first**—particularly if public-interest/public-service work is a serious possibility. Its **PIPS** application has a separate **January 31** deadline for the Fall 2027 cycle, while its JD application opens September 1, 2026. Ask Admissions to confirm the PIPS application materials, selection timing, and how it interacts with other aid. The office identifies Alex Richmond as the PIPS contact, but the page gives two versions of the PIPS email; I would use the JD office’s main address, **wcladmit@wcl.american.edu**, and/or phone them to avoid a typo issue.

## 1) Maryland Carey Law (Baltimore)

**Contact / meeting**
- Admissions: **admissions@law.umaryland.edu** | **410-706-3492**
- Hours: Monday–Friday, 9 a.m.–5 p.m.
- The visits page offers campus visits, tours, class visits, webinars/workshops, and a virtual tour.
- Links: [Contact Admissions](https://www.law.umaryland.edu/admissions--aid/contact-admissions/) · [Visits & Events](https://www.law.umaryland.edu/admissions--aid/visits--events/)

**Online event coming up**
- Its posted JD calendar lists a **Personal Statement Workshop, July 22, 2026, noon–1 p.m.**, followed by a **JD Admissions 101 Webinar, August 13, 2026, noon–1 p.m.** Registration links are on the calendar.
- Link: [JD webinars calendar](https://www.law.umaryland.edu/admissions--aid/visits--events/jd-webinars/)

**Funding**
- JD applicants are automatically considered for the **Maryland Law Scholars Program** (merit scholarships).
- Need-based aid can include grants, loans, and/or work-study; FAFSA is required for aid to post, using UMB school code **002104**.
- Carey says its merit scholarships are renewable while the recipient stays in good academic and character standing, and that it does **not** offer conditional scholarships.
- It also lists public-interest loan-repayment assistance and Yellow Ribbon participation for eligible veterans/active-duty students.
- Link: [Scholarships & Aid](https://www.law.umaryland.edu/admissions--aid/scholarships--aid/)

## 2) University of Baltimore School of Law (Baltimore Law / UBalt)

**Contact / meeting**
- Office of Law Admissions: **lawadmissions@ubalt.edu** | **410-837-4459**
- Hours: Monday–Friday, 8:30 a.m.–4:30 p.m.
- You can schedule a **30-minute phone/Zoom appointment**, an individual **in-person tour**, and optionally a meeting with an admissions counselor alongside the tour.
- Links: [Admissions & Aid](https://www.ubalt.edu/law/admission-and-aid/index.cfm) · [Visits, Tours & Events](https://www.ubalt.edu/law/admission-and-aid/visit/index.cfm)

**Online event coming up**
- **Fall Virtual Open House — Tuesday, October 27, 2026, 6–7 p.m. ET via Zoom.** The school says no registration is required; the Zoom password listed is **UBaltLaw**.
- Link: [UBalt visits/events page](https://www.ubalt.edu/law/admission-and-aid/visit/index.cfm)

**Funding**
- UBalt reports that **67%** of accepted students in its 2025 entering class received scholarship or grant funding.
- Its scholarship page search result reports average awards of **$10,000 in-state** and **$24,000 out-of-state**. Confirm current award practices and renewal terms directly with Admissions, since the school has recently redesigned parts of its site.
- It also has public-interest funding resources for students/graduates pursuing public-service careers.
- Start with: [Admissions & Aid](https://www.ubalt.edu/law/admission-and-aid/index.cfm)

## 3) American University Washington College of Law (DC)

**Contact / meeting**
- JD Admissions: **wcladmit@wcl.american.edu** | **202-274-4101**
- Office: 4300 Nebraska Ave. NW, Suite C201, Washington, DC 20016.
- Admissions offers virtual appointments. Joseph Benge’s booking page is linked from the visits page; Alex Richmond also has a virtual-appointment link and is identified as the PIPS admissions contact.
- Links: [Campus & Virtual Visits](https://www.american.edu/wcl/school/admissions/jd-admissions/campus-virtual-visits/) · [Admissions contacts](https://www.american.edu/wcl/school/admissions/jd-admissions/contact-us.cfm)

**Online event coming up**
- **Virtual Information Sessions:** most Tuesdays at **3 p.m. ET**, September 15–November 17, led by an admissions staff member and current law student. Register at least one business day ahead for the Zoom link.
- Link: [Campus & Virtual Visits](https://www.american.edu/wcl/school/admissions/jd-admissions/campus-virtual-visits/)

**Funding, including PIPS**
- **PIPS = Public Interest/Public Service Scholarship.** WCL describes it as a scholarship for **incoming, full-time 1L JD students**, with a **separate application** required. The school’s admissions materials describe PIPS as a three-year, full-tuition public-interest/public-service scholarship.
- For the Fall 2027 cycle, WCL’s published timeline lists **January 31** for PIPS. Because this is a separate scholarship process and an early deadline, it is the main reason I would call WCL first.
- WCL’s timeline says initial merit-scholarship notices begin in **mid-February**. It lists **March 1** as the deadline for both the WCL institutional need-based-aid application and FAFSA.
- Link: [WCL admissions timeline and requirements](https://www.american.edu/wcl/school/admissions/jd/apply/first-year/requirements.cfm)

### Suggested first email/call question to WCL
“I'm considering applying as a full-time JD candidate with a public-interest focus. Could you confirm the PIPS application requirements, whether PIPS can be combined with any other WCL aid, when decisions are expected, and who should receive my questions?”

That gets you the time-sensitive PIPS answer first, while still leaving time to arrange the Carey and UBalt conversations.
